osaka_tako_ume_honten_dotonbori.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. The oden simmers in one shared broth with fish cakes, shumai and tempura-style items alongside daikon, egg and konnyaku, and the octopus is simmered sweet in the house broth; nothing is described as gluten-free.
osaka_tako_ume_honten_dotonbori.vegan_detail: Not vegan: every oden item is simmered in the house broth, which takes its depth from whale tongue (official site).
osaka_tako_ume_honten_dotonbori.hours_raw: Daily 16:00–21:50, last order 21:30 — shortened since 20 February 2024 for lack of staff; closed 31 December–3 January (Tabelog). Reservations by phone only, after 15:00; fan-club members book a month ahead, LINE members and others a week ahead; a booking for someone else is treated as a walk-in (Tabelog). Seat charge: an appetiser ¥275 a person (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR (Tabelog). 21 seats: a counter of 12 around the oden pot and tables for 9; non-smoking; English menu; children welcome, with care on the tall counter stools (Tabelog). Founded 1844 (official site).
osaka_tako_ume_honten_dotonbori.notes: [Oden · Dotonbori, since 1844] Calling itself the oldest oden shop in Japan, Tako Ume has simmered kanto-daki on Dotonbori since 1844, a counter of twelve around the oden pot and a window at the back onto the river. The broth takes its depth from saezuri, whale tongue, which the founder first used; order it, with the tako kanroni of sweet simmered octopus eaten with mustard, then daikon, potato, egg and the seasonal items, and a cup of sake warmed in tin. Writers from 織田作之助 to 開高健 ate here (official site). Budget ¥3,000–8,000 in 2026, plus a ¥275 appetiser; book by phone after 15:00. Open 16:00–21:50 daily.

roles: Fifth-generation owner (official site)
Founder: 岡田梅次郎 (official site)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: an oden and sake house ("上燗屋") open since 1844 on Dotonbori, now in its fifth generation, from the founder 岡田梅次郎 to 岡田哲生, and called the oldest oden shop in Japan. The founder first used saezuri, whale tongue, which gives its kanto-daki a deep flavour; baleen-whale tongue is still bought and prepared in house, and the tako kanroni of madako has been simmered in the traditional broth since the start. Sake is warmed in tin tanpo in hot water and served in tin cups. Writers including 織田作之助, 池波正太郎, 檀一雄, 田辺聖子 and 吉田健一 were customers, and 開高健, a customer from the grandfather's day, wrote ten pages on Tako Ume in a novel. The current owner recalls an uncle, the previous owner, saying the shop lasted a hundred years because parents bring their children, who later bring theirs; that memory, on a hard winter night after the Lehman shock, set the aim of keeping the shop for the next hundred years.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Keep a place where parents bring their children, for the next hundred years" (official site, translated).
chef_bio.specialty: Saezuri (whale tongue) oden; tako kanroni.

anecdotes.text: "The interior hasn't changed much at all; it still has the atmosphere of the Taisho era, not just Showa. The copper sake warming stand is the same as well." — June 2026, a first visit in 15 years.
"When I opened the window at the back, I could see the Dotonbori River flowing by" — June 2026.
"They were about to flip the sign to closed, but they let us in with the promise that our first order would be our last order." — August 2026, tako kanroni and whale saezuri, JPY 6,105 for two.

osaka_odoriya_nishinakajima.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. Sashimi and nigiri come with soy sauce, and kara-age, tempura, chicken nanban, Taiwanese menchi katsu and cha soba are on the menu. One June 2026 group had its banquet course adjusted for dietary restrictions, so ask when booking.
osaka_odoriya_nishinakajima.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a seafood and robata izakaya with fish, meat and seafood hot pots. Tabelog ticks "vegetarian options" but names none.
osaka_odoriya_nishinakajima.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 17:00–24:00 (food last order 23:00, drinks 23:30); holidays and the day before a holiday 17:00–24:00; closed Sunday, with substitute days off when a holiday falls; New Year opening from 5 January (Tabelog). Reservations accepted; walk-ins found room at 19:00 on a June 2026 night (half full). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR (Tabelog). 46 seats with a counter, tatami and sunken seating, semi-private seats for 2 to 30, whole hire for 20–50; non-smoking (Tabelog).
osaka_odoriya_nishinakajima.notes: [Izakaya · Nishinakajima, market fish and hot-pot banquets] A 46-seat seafood and robata izakaya between Shin-Osaka and Nishinakajima-Minamigata, with a counter for one and tatami rooms for office parties. The shop buys fish every morning at the central market, and its five-kind sashimi platter (¥748 a head) is on nearly every table. Banquet courses (¥5,300–6,500 with drinks) run sashimi, fried dishes and a hot pot of shrimp, clams and sea bream, then a big seafood maki roll; one June 2026 group had its course adjusted for dietary needs. Alone at the counter you can order single pieces of nigiri at ¥250 and a plate of Taiwanese menchi katsu (August 2026). Diners mention a homey feel and attentive staff (2026). Closed Sundays.

roles: Kitchen and floor staff (unnamed)
chef_bio.background: Per the shop-maintained Tabelog listing: fresh seafood bought each morning at the central market, "We don't just rely on freshness; we carefully select ingredients every morning"; a five-kind sashimi platter ordered by almost every table; hamo suki nabe; private dining for 2 to 30. Per reviews: friendly staff and great service (April 2026); "the staff were quite attentive" (June 2026); "a very homey atmosphere" (October 2026).
chef_bio.specialty: Five-kind sashimi platter; seafood hot-pot courses.

anecdotes.text: "You can order just one piece of nigiri, and it was fresh and delicious." — August 2026, alone at the counter; squid, sea bream and horse mackerel at ¥250 each.
"We enjoyed the All-You-Can-Drink Market Banquet Course, which was slightly modified due to some dietary restrictions." — June 2026.

osaka_ramenza_yuto_nishinakajima.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: thick or thin wheat noodles in a soy-based Jiro-style broth or abura soba sauce.
osaka_ramenza_yuto_nishinakajima.vegan_detail: Not vegan: niboshi, bonito and tonkotsu broths with back fat and pork chashu.
osaka_ramenza_yuto_nishinakajima.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–15:00 (last order 14:40) and 18:00–23:00 (last order 22:30); hours may change (Tabelog). Buy a ticket at the machine by the door; it took no new banknotes in July 2025. Cash only (Tabelog). 20 seats, all at tables (three for four, one for eight), shared at busy times; non-smoking (Tabelog). Lunch fills with office workers and lines form outside (September 2026); after 13:30 it is quiet (September 2026). The 10th of each month is "Yuto Day", with a voucher for the next visit (September 2026). Opened 22 June 2021 (Tabelog).
osaka_ramenza_yuto_nishinakajima.notes: [Ramen · Nishinakajima-Minamigata, Jiro-style niboshi bowls] A 20-seat ramen shop among the restaurants of Nishinakajima-Minamigata, open since 2021, serving Jiro-style bowls with a niboshi (dried sardine) or bonito broth: thick chewy noodles under a heap of bean sprouts and cabbage, back fat and grilled chashu, with noodle weight, vegetables, fat and sauce chosen when you hand over your ticket. Garlic is only added on request, and cayenne pepper on the table is the house twist. Bowls run about ¥1,000; the abura soba ends with rice and a raw egg in the bowl. One diner traced the bowl to a shop in Abeno Lucias that closed in January 2024 and found the same dish here (April 2024). Opinions split on the fish broth: "strong niboshi flavor" to one (September 2026), powdery to another (August 2026). Cash only; lunch lines form.

roles: Owner-chef (unnamed) and one floor staff member (July 2025, September 2026 reviews)
chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog listing: opened 22 June 2021. Per reviews: "two staff members—one female and the owner—serving" (July 2025); "one busy chef in the kitchen and one male staff member managing the dining area" at a September 2026 lunch; a diner who had eaten the same niboshi Jiro-style bowl at a shop in the Abeno Lucias basement, closed 27 January 2024, found it here (April 2024 and September 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: Jiro-style niboshi ramen; abura soba.

anecdotes.text: "Halfway through, I sprinkled on some cayenne pepper, which is a unique feature of this shop." — September 2026.
"The same dish I had at Lucias was served … it might just be a matter of crossing the Yodogawa River to get here instead." — April 2024.
"Garlic is not included by default, so there's no need to worry about the smell. Perhaps that's why there were many salarymen dining here." — September 2026.

osaka_teuchi_men_yasuda_shin_osaka.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: thick handmade wheat noodles with kansui (October 2026), in a shio or shoyu broth.
osaka_teuchi_men_yasuda_shin_osaka.vegan_detail: Not vegan: iriko (dried sardine) and bonito broths with pork chashu.
osaka_teuchi_men_yasuda_shin_osaka.hours_raw: Tue–Sun 11:30–14:30, until sold out; closed Monday, plus irregular days and frequent temporary closures (Tabelog). One November 2026 diner had found it closed several times; another found it open at 14:00 (October 2026), and one Saturday it opened at 11:19 with five already seated (October 2026). Expect a short wait at noon: 10–20 minutes in October 2026. Order by telling the owner and pay after (October 2026). Cash only (Tabelog). 7 counter seats; table seats closed since March 2019, when the owner began running the shop alone (Tabelog). Non-smoking, ashtray at the door (Tabelog). English menu (Tabelog). No large size; no tsukemen (October 2026; Tabelog). Opened 13 September 2011 (Tabelog).
osaka_teuchi_men_yasuda_shin_osaka.notes: [Ramen · Shin-Osaka east side, one man and seven seats] A seven-seat counter four minutes from the Shin-Osaka east exit, open since 2011 and in Tabelog's Ramen 100 every year from 2017 to 2025. Since 2019 the owner has run it alone, making the noodles by hand, cooking, serving and taking cash; one October 2026 diner wrote of "respect" for the solo operation. The noodles are the point: thick, curly and chewy, "about the thickness of a disposable chopstick" and close to udon (October 2026), in a clear, gentle shio broth of iriko, with green and white onion, menma and pork-belly chashu, ¥900. Add katsuo rice for ¥200. Lunch only, until the noodles run out, and it often closes without notice, so have a backup. Cash only; no large size.

roles: Owner (unnamed), runs the shop alone since March 2019 (Tabelog)
chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog listing (remarks): "Due to focusing on ramen, we are not serving tsukemen. We often have temporary closures. As of March 2019, the owner is handling everything alone, so we have closed the table seating and are only offering counter seating." Opened 13 September 2011; Tabelog Ramen 100 (WEST 2017–2022, OSAKA 2023–2025). Per reviews: "The owner operates the restaurant solo, skillfully handling the noodle draining, bowls, and toppings" (June 2025); "The owner was running the place solo" (October 2026).
chef_bio.specialty: Handmade thick curly noodles; iriko shio ramen.

anecdotes.text: "They are about the thickness of a disposable chopstick, making me wonder if they were udon … However, they seem to have kansui added, giving them a slight yellow tint." — October 2026, shio ramen ¥900 and katsuo rice ¥200.

"Although the opening time is supposed to be 11:30, [the shop] opened at 11:19, and there were already five customers seated at the counter." — October 2026, a Saturday.

osaka_vege_cafe_plus_alpha_nishinakajima.gf_detail: Ask. A December 2025 review shows a vegan soup-curry plate captioned as free of the 28 specified allergens and gluten-free (アレルギー特定原材料28品目不使用。グルテンフリー。), served with rice-flour bread, and the cafe serves rice-flour cookies (June 2026). But the shop's own text promises allergy-friendly gelato, not gluten-free food, and the cafe bakes wheat bread on site (whole-grain rolls, natural-yeast breads), so ask what is gluten-free today and how it is kept apart.
osaka_vege_cafe_plus_alpha_nishinakajima.vegan_detail: The shop says its gelato "caters to vegans and those with allergies" (Tabelog). A December 2025 review shows a vegan soup-curry plate with rice-flour bread. Lunch (fried fish, scrambled egg) and the breakfast sandwiches are not vegan; ask which gelato flavours are vegan that day.
osaka_vege_cafe_plus_alpha_nishinakajima.hours_raw: Tue–Sat 09:00–17:00 (food last order 16:00, drinks 16:30); lunch 11:00–14:00 until sold out; closed Sunday, Monday and holidays (Tabelog). The limited "Vege Cafe Kago Gozen" lunch is best booked; at busy times a 90-minute limit (Tabelog). Walk-ins at 11:00 on a Saturday got in (May 2026). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX) and e-money; no service charge (Tabelog). 49 seats: 6 at the counter, 43 at tables, a semi-private room for up to 15, whole hire for 20–50; non-smoking indoors, smoking only on the terrace (Tabelog). Pets on the open terrace only, not when it rains; children welcome, child-friendly dishes, no high chairs; free Wi-Fi; wheelchair accessible; English menu (Tabelog). A takeaway gelato and coffee window faces the street (May 2026).
osaka_vege_cafe_plus_alpha_nishinakajima.notes: [Cafe · Nishinakajima, vegetables, bread and gelato] A roomy 49-seat cafe in the Nishinakajima office district, a seven-minute walk from Nishinakajima-Minamigata, that grows organic vegetables on its rooftop and makes its own gelato, prized three years running at an Italian competition (Tabelog). Mornings bring natural-yeast breads and sandwiches on whole-grain rolls; at lunch the limited "Kago Gozen" basket (¥1,350) sets a main of the day beside small vegetable sides, salad and soup, so book. The shop says its gelato suits vegans and people with allergies, and a December 2025 diner had a vegan soup-curry plate with rice-flour bread. Seasonal decorations, a mix of tables and chairs, a courtyard terrace where dogs are welcome. Closed Sundays, Mondays and holidays.

roles: Kitchen and floor staff (unnamed)
chef_bio.background: Per the shop-maintained Tabelog listing: a cafe focused on "food", "vegetables" and "space", with organic vegetables grown on the rooftop and a healthy, vegetable-rich menu; a gelato shop added in July 2020, whose gelato "caters to vegans and those with allergies" and "has won awards for three consecutive years at the world's most prestigious gelato competition". Per reviews: bread baked on site (October 2026); the staff speak "in a soothing manner" (October 2026); "the staff had a warm atmosphere" (July 2026).

chef_bio.specialty: Kago Gozen vegetable lunch; house gelato.

"This gelato is an award-winning flavor from the world's toughest gelato competition in Italy." — October 2026, organic apple balsamic and mascarpone.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (店舗会員): vegecafe＋α、カフェ・野菜料理・ジェラート、大阪市淀川区西中島6-9-20 新大阪GHビル 1F、西中島南方駅から徒歩7分、火〜土9:00〜17:00、ランチ11:00〜14:00 (売り切れまで)、日・月・祝休み、予約可、混雑時は1.5時間制、カード・電子マネー可、サービス料なし、49席、テラスのみ喫煙可、ペットはテラス席のみ、子ども可、Wi-Fi、英語メニュー。店の紹介: 屋上で無農薬の野菜を育てる、2020年7月からジェラートの店、ジェラートはヴィーガンやアレルギーの人にも、世界的なジェラートの大会で3年連続入賞。口コミ(2025年12月〜2026年10月): 桐生酵母全粒粉ロール使用 生ハムレタスチーズサンド900円、珈琲セット (+400円)、天然酵母パン3種640円、veganスープカレープレート (アレルギー特定原材料28品目不使用、グルテンフリー) と米粉パン、Kago Gozen 1,350円、アジフライとからしのタルタル、バスクチーズケーキ、米粉のクッキー、テイクアウトの窓口でコーヒーフロート、りんごのバルサミコとマスカルポーネのジェラート。

osaka_konamon_mitsukuni_uranamba.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: the okonomiyaki batter is 100% Japanese wheat (official site), the yakisoba and modern-yaki use wheat noodles, and the monjayaki is a flour batter. The menu marks allergens with pictograms, so ask staff about any side dish.
osaka_konamon_mitsukuni_uranamba.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the okonomiyaki batter is made with a Kyoto-style bonito dashi (official site), and the fillings are pork, seafood, egg and cheese.
osaka_konamon_mitsukuni_uranamba.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–15:00 (last order 14:00) and 17:00–23:00 (last order 22:00); no closing day (official site; Tabelog). Lunch is limited to 90 minutes and takes no courses; when busy, dinner seats are limited to two hours (official site). Reservations online or by phone; on-the-day booking worked on a weekday (2026 reviews); in September 2026 two walk-in groups were turned away. Each guest orders at least one drink and one dish; no outside drinks (official site). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners, Discover), IC cards, e-money and QR (official site; Tabelog). 40 seats, all at sunken horigotatsu tables (September 2026 review); a heated-tobacco-only smoking area; private hire possible (Tabelog). Upstairs on 2F, up stairs that one diner found steep (Google review quoted on the official site). Children welcome (Tabelog).
osaka_konamon_mitsukuni_uranamba.notes: [Okonomiyaki · Ura Namba, okonomiyaki and creative monja with wine] Up a flight of stairs in Ura Namba, a calm Japanese room of sunken horigotatsu tables that bills itself as an "upmarket" okonomiyaki house and, as one diner found, is one of the few that take bookings. The head chef's okonomiyaki uses 100% Japanese wheat and a Kyoto-style bonito dashi and comes fluffy, loaded with shrimp and scallops; the yakisoba and modern-yaki use fresh noodles from the noodle works behind the shop, which several diners rate as the real star. The monjayaki go far from the classic, cooked for you at the table: basil Genovese, white miso with mochi, mapo, ebi-chili, bibimbap. Plenty of side dishes for drinking, all of the KENZO ESTATE wines and Japanese whisky. Tabelog Okonomiyaki 100 in 2025. Book ahead (walk-ins were turned away on a September 2026 night); open daily for lunch and dinner to 23:00.

roles: Head chef (unnamed; 料理長 on the official site)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: the head chef spent years eating around restaurants before deciding to cook, and worked out the batter and the cooking through trial and error; the yakisoba noodles come from the noodle works that is the shop's parent company. The site stocks every KENZO ESTATE wine. Tabelog Okonomiyaki 100, 2025. No opening date or owner is given.
chef_bio.philosophy: A "one rank above" okonomiyaki house: ingredients, technique and taste pursued to their limit (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Seafood okonomiyaki; creative monjayaki; fresh-noodle yakisoba.

anecdotes.text: "On this day alone, two groups were turned away." — September 2026, mozzarella okonomiyaki.
"The okonomiyaki was incredibly fluffy and delicious, but the yakisoba was the real star—thick noodles with a chewy texture" — October 2026, a weekday walk-in.
"It felt like there were many international customers." — October 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (konamondokoro-mitsukuni.com): 粉もん處 光圀 裏なんば店、大阪難波・千日前にあるワンランク上のお好み焼き店、料理長が試行錯誤を重ねた特製レシピ、国産小麦を100%使用、香り豊かな京風の鰹出汁、グラタン・黒ごま坦々・ジェノベーゼなど約10種類のもんじゃ焼き、店舗の母体である製麺所から直送の焼きそば専用の生麺、ケンゾーエステートのワインを全種類、響・山崎・白州、掘りごたつ式のテーブル席、難波千日前3-18 中村ビル 2F、11:00-15:00 (L.O.14:00)・17:00-23:00 (L.O.22:00)、ランチはコース不可、定休日なし、カード・電子マネー・交通系IC可。メニュー: 1人1ドリンク1フード、日本円かカード、混雑時は2時間、ランチは90分制、アレルギーのピクトグラム、ぶた玉1,300円、えび玉1,800円、ほたて玉2,000円、モッツァレラ玉1,900円、海鮮スペシャル2,700円、生麺モダン ぶた1,600円〜海鮮スペシャル3,000円、ジェノベーゼもんじゃ2,700円、とろけるお餅の白味噌みつくにもんじゃ2,800円、四川麻婆もんじゃ2,600円。食べログ (店舗会員): お好み焼き 百名店 2025、40席、加熱式たばこのみの喫煙所、貸切可、子ども可。口コミ(2026年9月〜10月): 予約がおすすめ、全席掘りごたつ、海鮮たっぷり、ふわふわの生地、太くもちもちの焼きそば、もんじゃは店の人が焼く、ジェノベーゼ、コースと飲み放題、海外からの客も多い。

cultural_comfort.note: The official site has an English page; staff cook the monja at the table; many overseas guests (October 2026).

osaka_wagyu_yakiniku_gin_namba.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. The meat comes with the house-made tare and the yukhoe with a sauce; salt-grilled tongue and plain rice are the simplest, but nothing is described as gluten-free.
osaka_wagyu_yakiniku_gin_namba.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a wagyu yakiniku restaurant; the courses are built on beef, with kimchi, namul and salad as starters.
osaka_wagyu_yakiniku_gin_namba.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 17:00–23:00; Sat–Sun 16:00–23:00; last orders food 22:00, drinks 22:30 (official site). Tabelog adds a weekend and holiday lunch from 12:00; closed 31 December–1 January (Tabelog). Reservations; a same-day cancellation fee applies (Tabelog); one diner found private rooms reserved for course bookings (October 2026). A service charge on à la carte orders, not on courses (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners, UnionPay), IC cards, e-money and QR including Alipay and WeChat Pay (Tabelog). 80 seats in 25 private rooms for 2 to 16, some with sofas or sunken horigotatsu, with night views; non-smoking (Tabelog). On the 10th floor of Namba HIPS, linked underground to Namba Stn exit 15-B (Tabelog; official site). Opened 15 April 2015; renewed 10 June 2025 (Tabelog; official site).
osaka_wagyu_yakiniku_gin_namba.notes: [Yakiniku · Namba, private-room wagyu above the station] On the 10th floor of Namba HIPS, reached from Namba station without going outside, 25 private rooms of two to sixteen seats, many with a night view. The pitch is A5 kuroge wagyu and Kobe beef at low prices (cuts from ¥680), and a raw-meat licence for its signature wagyu mille-feuille yukhoe, layered with green onion and mixed with egg yolk. Rice is cooked to order pot by pot, best with wagyu and ikura on top. Weeknight courses start at ¥5,000 for ten dishes (Tuesday to Thursday), with all-you-can-drink for ¥2,000 more. Diners in 2026 praise the value and the privacy for dates and celebrations; one found the grilled cuts only average and the room dark. Renewed in June 2025. Tabelog Yakiniku WEST 100 in 2022.

chef_bio.background: Per the official site: aims to be the best-value yakiniku in Japan for A5 kuroge wagyu and Kobe beef; licensed to serve raw meat; rice cooked to order in individual pots; renewed and reopened on 10 June 2025. Opened 15 April 2015 (Tabelog). Tabelog Yakiniku WEST 100, 2022. No owner or chef is named.
chef_bio.specialty: Wagyu mille-feuille yukhoe; thick-cut tongue; pot-cooked rice with wagyu and ikura.

anecdotes.text: "An unusual combination was the ikura (salmon roe) with wagyu rice, which surprisingly worked well together." — October 2026, a first visit.
"It seems that the private room can only be reserved by those who order the course meal." — October 2026.
"As for the grilled meats, I found them to be just average." — October 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (gin-nanba.com): 個室 和牛焼肉 吟〜ぎん〜、難波1-8-16 難波HIPS 10F、なんば駅15B出口すぐ (地下鉄連絡通路直結)、月〜金 17:00〜23:00、土日 16:00〜23:00 (料理L.O.22:00、ドリンクL.O.22:30)、2025年6月10日リニューアルOPEN、A5ランク黒毛和牛が680円 (税込748円) から、日本一お値打ちを目指す神戸牛、名物のタン、生食許可店の和牛ミルフィーユユッケ、一釜ずつ炊き上げる贅沢炊き立て銀シャリ。お品書き: 火〜木限定の彩コース5,000円 (吟名物 生キムチ、ナムル2種盛り、本日のサラダ、生せんまい・ハツ刺し、炊き立て吟シャリ、牛タン塩、本日の和牛2種、神戸牛 吟 特選すき焼きカルビ、りんごハラミ (豚)、本日のアイス)、和コース6,000円 (和牛赤身炙り寿司、神戸牛出汁しゃぶカルビ、ユッケジャンクッパなど)、竹コース7,000円、飲み放題はプラス2,000円。食べログ (店舗会員): 焼肉・ホルモン・ステーキ、全室個室 (25室、2〜16名)、80席、夜景、禁煙、別途サービス料 (コースは不要)、当日キャンセル料、土日祝はランチも、2015年4月15日オープン、焼肉 WEST 百名店 2022。口コミ(2026年9月〜10月): 上タン、和牛ミルフィーユユッケ、和牛といくらの吟シャリ、コースの値打ち、個室はコース予約のみという声、焼いた肉はふつうという声も。

osaka_sakuichi_honten.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information. A kappo built around fish: sashimi, grilled fish and plain-cooked seasonal produce are on the long à la carte menu, but tempura, fried fugu and katsu are wheat, and soy sauce and dashi-based seasonings are used throughout.
osaka_sakuichi_honten.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a fish-led Japanese kitchen with dashi-based dishes; vegetables appear mainly as seasonal sides.
osaka_sakuichi_honten.hours_raw: Mon–Sat from 17:00; the official site gives 17:00–22:00 with last orders (drinks included) at 21:30 since March 2022, while Tabelog lists 17:00–24:00. Closed Sunday and the third Monday of each month (official notice, from February 2024). Reservations; walk-ins possible (April 2026). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) and e-money; no QR; no service charge (Tabelog). 40 seats on the 3rd and 4th floors: an 8-seat counter, private rooms for 2 to 8 including horigotatsu rooms; smoking allowed on the 3rd floor and in a two-person room on the 4th (Tabelog). The entrance is on the 4th floor (September 2025). The sister counter 弘作一 is on the ground floor of the same building (official site).
osaka_sakuichi_honten.notes: [Kappo · Shinsaibashi, a long-running Osaka kappo with a metre-long menu] On the upper floors of a building behind the Nikko Hotel Osaka, a quiet kappo that has cooked in Minami for more than 40 years and moved here from 三津寺筋 in October 2002. The rooms, designed by 喜多俊之 of IDKデザイン on a theme of medieval Naniwa, run from an eight-seat counter where the owner cooks to private rooms for two to eight. The joy is the handwritten menu of the day, over a metre of washi listing seasonal fish and vegetables, from which you choose and say how you would like it cooked: Yura sea urchin, Biwa ayu, firefly-squid risotto in spring; matsutake picked from a basket, dobin-mushi, mackerel bōzushi in autumn. A course runs from ¥15,000. Long a favourite for business dinners; expect ¥20,000–¥30,000 a head. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.chef_name: 奥長弘一 (as written; no romaji given)
roles: 主人 (owner) of 作一 (official notices, signed 主人 奥長弘一)

chef_bio.background: Per the official site: Sakuichi has traded for more than 40 years and now has two shops in one building, 作一本店 on the 3rd and 4th floors and 弘作一 on the ground floor (renewed on 12 June 2020); the main shop moved from 三津寺筋 in October 2002, with interiors by 喜多俊之 of IDKデザイン on the theme of "medieval Naniwa"; the owner cooks at the counter with the season's produce. A March 2026 diner on a fifth visit, and others since 2022, describe choosing dishes and cooking styles with the chef across the counter.
chef_bio.philosophy: "作一に行けば、本物が食べられる" — go to Sakuichi and you eat the real thing (official site tagline); a quiet place to ease the day's fatigue (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Seasonal fish chosen from the daily menu; sashimi platters; mackerel bōzushi.

anecdotes.text: "The menu, written on a washi paper over a meter long, lists seasonal ingredients alongside classic dishes, making it a joy to discuss and decide what to eat today." — March 2026, a fifth visit.
"I have fond memories of this place from my days working at a major securities firm, where I visited many times for business dinners." — August 2026.
"I was allowed to choose from a basket of Iwate matsutake mushrooms" — October 2025.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (sakuichi.com): 作一、日本料理、作一に行けば、本物が食べられる、40年以上営業、同じビルに2つの店、作一本店 (3・4階、完全個室、4階2名・4名、3階6名・8名)、弘作一 (1階、2020年6月12日新装開店、店長 河村幸貴、主人 奥長弘一)、2002年10月に三津寺筋より移店、IDKデザインの喜多俊之さんのコンセプトは「日本、浪速の中世」、カウンターでは店主みずからが四季折々の旬の素材で腕を振るう、西心斎橋1-10-3 エースビル3・4階、2022年3月22日から17時〜22時 (L.O.21時30分)、2024年2月から定休日は日曜日と第三月曜日、コース15,000円〜 (前菜、お造り、煮物、酢の物、焼き物又は揚げ物、和え物、八寸盛り、季節のごはん・釜飯、デザート)、季節のおすすめ (2026年11月): 子持ち本ししゃも一夜干し、秋サバの棒ずし。食べログ (店舗会員): 日本料理、40席 (カウンター8、個室)、3階と4階の2名個室は喫煙可、カード・電子マネー可、サービス料なし。口コミ(2025年9月〜2026年8月): 1メートル以上の和紙のお品書き、好きな素材と調理法を選べる、お造りの盛り合わせ、松茸を籠から選ぶ、土瓶蒸し、鯖の棒ずし、ふぐの唐揚げ、接待に、Nikko Hotel Osaka の裏、入口は4階。

cultural_comfort.note: A long handwritten Japanese menu; order by talking with the chef or staff. No English evidence found.

osaka_deux_ash_higashishinsaibashi.gf_detail: Ask when booking. The listing asks guests to state allergies and dislikes in advance and says same-day requests may not be possible. Courses include homemade bread, granita, and a dessert tree; nothing is described as gluten-free.
osaka_deux_ash_higashishinsaibashi.vegan_detail: Ask when booking. Tabelog lists vegetarian options, and the kitchen adjusted a main course for a guest who does not eat much meat (August 2026); no vegan course is listed.
osaka_deux_ash_higashishinsaibashi.hours_raw: Tue–Sun lunch 11:30–15:00 (last order 13:30), dinner 17:30–22:30 (last order 21:00); closed Monday, and from the third Monday to Wednesday of each month (official site). Tabelog gives last orders of 13:00 for lunch food and 20:00 for dinner food. Courses only; prices include tax and the 10% service charge (official site; Tabelog). Reservations; state allergies and dislikes (oysters, raw fish, shellfish, foie gras) in advance (Tabelog). At least one drink per guest (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) and PayPay; no e-money (Tabelog). 36 seats with a counter, parties up to 24, private rooms for 4 to 20 with no room charge but course minimums (lunch from ¥7,800, dinner from ¥12,800) (Tabelog). Children only in private rooms; a children's meal ¥2,800 booked the day before (Tabelog). Up to three hours in the ABC Motor Pool across from the entrance, north of Minami Elementary School (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog).
osaka_deux_ash_higashishinsaibashi.notes: [French · Higashi-Shinsaibashi, courses in a former securities office] Through a heavy door, past the old vault door kept from the building's days as a securities company, a high-ceilinged room with a single tree reaching up from a stone floor laid like a river, and private rooms on a mezzanine. The courses change with the season, from an eight-dish lunch at ¥5,900 to a chef's surprise menu at ¥16,500, all with tax and service included, and end at the dessert tree, where you pick from about eight desserts, as many as you like (one diner who was full got tiny portions of each). Service is warm and funny: diners in 2026 describe staff and a sommelier who joke, remember returning guests, cut the lamb at the table and explain each dish. A favourite for birthdays and family celebrations; children are welcome in private rooms. Closed Mondays and the third Monday to Wednesday.

roles: Chef (料理長, unnamed; official site)
Manager and sommelier (unnamed; 2026 reviews)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site, run under the name Cabinet2'H (copyright 2005–2009); courses only, prices including service and tax; staff recruitment notice and an Instagram account (site news, March 2026). The listing is shop-maintained (corporate member) and says the kitchen is particular about vegetables and fish.

osaka_tenhana_whity_umeda.vegan_detail: Not vegan: seafood and vegetable tempura from shared oil, with dipping sauce, red miso soup and whitebait in the sets.
osaka_tenhana_whity_umeda.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–22:00, last order 21:15; lunch 11:00–15:00, standing bar 15:00–22:00 (Tabelog); the listing text also says weekday lunch until 14:00 and standing drinks from 11:00 at weekends. Lunch sets only at lunch; at night tempura is ordered piece by piece, and rice and miso soup à la carte (September 2026). No reservations (Tabelog). No service charge (Tabelog's original text: 無し). Cards, e-money and QR (Tabelog); PayPay (September 2026). 11 seats at a U-shaped counter at lunch, about 18 standing places at night; some nights chairs are put out (December 2025). Non-smoking; school-age children welcome (Tabelog). Opened 20 February 2025 (Tabelog; press release).
osaka_tenhana_whity_umeda.notes: [Tempura · Umeda underground, a tempura counter in Whity] A small U-shaped counter in the Whity Umeda underground mall where tempura is fried a few pieces at a time in front of you, from seafood bought each morning at Osaka Kizu Market. Gourmet Kineya opened it in February 2025 as a tempura izakaya named after the market. At lunch, a set of seven pieces (shrimp, cod, scallop, eggplant, pepper, daikon and red pickled ginger) with rice and red miso soup is ¥770, and the boiled whitebait is free to refill. After 15:00 it becomes a standing bar: a ¥500 plate of seven bite-size tempura, a ¥320 large shrimp, beer and Osaka sake, salt or curry salt to dip. A September 2026 diner found the pieces small but cheap; an October 2026 diner ate and drank four highballs for ¥2,000. One older regular says the same owner ran a tempura-bowl shop here twenty years ago (October 2026). No bookings.

roles: Counter staff of 株式会社グルメ杵屋レストラン (unnamed)
chef_bio.background: Per the Gourmet Kineya Restaurant press release (PR TIMES, 21 January 2025): a new izakaya format built on freshly fried tempura, opened at Whity Umeda on 20 February 2025, its main ingredients bought daily at Osaka Kizu Market; lunch sets of daily tempura named 「幸おとこ」 and 「幸むすめ」, free refills of boiled whitebait from the market, and bite-size tempura (豆天) at night. Per an October 2026 review: a regular of a cheap tempura-bowl shop here twenty years ago was told by staff that "the owner hasn't changed".

osaka_meishan_jizo_yokocho.gf_detail: Not gluten-free in practice: the listing says the shop cannot take allergy requests. The menu is Chinese dishes in soy-based sauces, ramen, dumplings, yurinchi and yuba tempura.
osaka_meishan_jizo_yokocho.vegan_detail: Not vegan: mapo tofu, yurinchi, shrimp dishes, dim sum and ramen; tofu and yuba appear across the menu but with meat and seafood, and the shop takes no dietary requests.
osaka_meishan_jizo_yokocho.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–22:00, last order 21:30 (Tabelog). Reservations accepted; allergy requests cannot be accommodated (Tabelog). Lunch set meals; happy hour with draft beer ¥308 and highballs ¥219 (Tabelog); a draft-beer senbero set ¥1,000 before 19:00 (October 2026). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners, UnionPay), IC cards and other e-money, QR payment including Alipay and WeChat Pay (Tabelog). 24 seats at a counter and tables; non-smoking (Tabelog). osaka_meishan_jizo_yokocho.notes: [Chinese · Umeda, tofu-and-yuba Chinese in Jizo Yokocho] The second shop of 梅香, a Chinese restaurant produced by the tofu-and-yuba chain Ume no Hana, opened in June 2025 in the Jizo Yokocho lane of Hankyu Sanbangai, a few steps from the Hankyu gates. Sets follow a one-soup, three-dish pattern and lean on the group's tofu and yuba: mapo tofu with a tofu salad, a soy-milk shrimp mayonnaise lighter than most, tofu shumai, yuba tempura. The favourite is yurinchi, fried chicken in a sweet-sour chilli sauce, alone or paired with mapo tofu in the ¥1,960 double-main set. Diners were mixed: good mapo and yurinchi, but a soggy fried rice, dishes that felt reheated and a cramped room (2026). Happy hour pours beer at ¥308. The shop cannot handle allergy requests.

osaka_sekai_no_wine_hakubutsukan_grand_f.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. The lunch buffet is pizza, paella, curry and fried mains such as cordon bleu, and courses include fried chicken and pasta; nothing is described as gluten-free.

osaka_sekai_no_wine_hakubutsukan_grand_f.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–23:00 (last order food 22:00, drinks 22:30); lunch menu 11:00–14:30; closed when the building closes (Tabelog). Weekday lunch buffet with no time limit (Tabelog); a diner had 90 minutes (October 2026). Reservations accepted; for two or more the course fee is charged on cancellation, 10% from booking rising to 100% three days before (Tabelog). Service charge 10% (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners), IC cards and other e-money, PayPay and other QR (Tabelog). 120 seats and a separate party room; private rooms for 4 to over 30; non-smoking, smoking room on the floor (Tabelog). Full of group bookings at 17:00 on a July 2026 weekday; quiet on a Saturday at 20:30 (August 2026). Opened 26 April 2013 (Tabelog).
osaka_sekai_no_wine_hakubutsukan_grand_f.notes: [Wine bar · Umekita, a big wine hall under Grand Front] A large, chandelier-lit wine restaurant in the basement of Grand Front Osaka's North Building, with sofa seats, private rooms and 120 seats, run by the ZATO group. Glasses come from a dispenser that keeps open bottles fresh, picked by a senior sommelier: Riesling, Napa Chardonnay, a sparkling wine with cherry-blossom petals (October 2026). Weekday lunch is a world buffet for ¥2,200, salad bar, pizza, paella and curry, plus a main from five countries such as cordon bleu or a cowboy steak. At night it fills with company parties on two-hour drink courses of charcuterie, Caesar salad, Italian fried chicken and roast pork from ¥4,500, the same courses as the neighbouring Sekai no Beer Hakubutsukan (August 2026). Book for evenings; a 10% service charge applies.

roles: Senior sommelier and kitchen staff (unnamed)

The operator's page (zato.co.jp, ZATO group) lists the Grand Front Osaka shop as its only 世界のワイン博物館. An August 2026 diner notes the courses match those of the nearby Sekai no Beer Hakubutsukan.

osaka_imai_kishou_ekimae_dai1.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. Seasonal Japanese dishes and rice bowls; soy-based sauces, Saikyo miso, tempura, cream croquettes and soba are on the menus, and nothing is described as gluten-free.
osaka_imai_kishou_ekimae_dai1.vegan_detail: Not vegan: sashimi, beef and fish dishes, dobin-mushi and miso soup; the vegetable dishes are not described as free of dashi.
osaka_imai_kishou_ekimae_dai1.hours_raw: Lunch Mon–Fri 12:00–14:00; dinner Mon–Fri 17:00–22:00 (last order 21:30); closed Saturdays, Sundays and holidays, with Sundays and holidays open for reservations only (official site). Tabelog instead gives Saturdays as reservation-only and Sundays and holidays closed, closures at Obon and New Year, and a summer opening at 16:00 for phone bookings; ask before a weekend visit. Booking early by phone is recommended (Tabelog). Cards (JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR (Tabelog). 20 seats: 10 at the counter and a table for up to 12; smoking allowed, though no one smoked on a March 2026 visit; BYO drinks (Tabelog). Opened 19 September 2012 (Tabelog).
osaka_imai_kishou_ekimae_dai1.notes: [Japanese · Umeda, a seasonal counter under the station buildings] A quiet Japanese restaurant at the far western end of the Osaka Ekimae Dai-1 Building basement, where "Ofukuro no Aji Imai", which fed office workers here for over forty years, merged with "Shiki no Aji Kishou" of the Tenjinbashi-suji arcade, whose chef Sato had cooked Japanese food for fifteen years (Tabelog). The site says the menu has changed every single day since opening. Lunch is a bargain: ¥1,000 for a Saga wagyu beef bowl, an oyako-don or a marinated seafood bowl, each with a small seasonal side dish, salad and soup. At night sit at the counter for sashimi, beef-tendon stew, cream croquettes or dobin-mushi, or book a course from ¥4,400. Diners call the chef imposing at first and chatty once the food comes out (July 2026); one found it pricey (March 2026). Smoking is allowed; weekends only by reservation, if at all.

roles: Chef, formerly of "Shiki no Aji Kishou" just off the Tenjinbashi-suji shopping street (Tabelog)
chef_bio.background: Per the shop-maintained Tabelog listing: "Ofukuro no Aji Imai" served salarymen after work at the Osaka Ekimae building for over forty years from the Showa era and became "Imai Kishou" by merging with "Shiki no Aji Kishou", led by Chef Sato, who has mastered Japanese cuisine for fifteen years, just off the Tenjinbashi-suji shopping street; opened 19 September 2012. Per the official site (copyright SANAE.inc): no day since opening without a change to the menu. A July 2025 diner saw the owner handling lunch alone; a March 2026 diner praises the woman serving.

osaka_kataoka_nikujirou_ekimae_dai2.notes: [Izakaya · Umeda, char siu and steak under the station buildings] A small meat bar in the basement of Osaka Ekimae Dai-2 Building, a minute from Kitashinchi Station, that pairs charcoal-grilled steak with Chinese food cooked by a chef of twenty years (Tabelog). Lunch is the draw: for ¥1,000, thick slabs of pork-belly char siu in a sweet sauce under two fried eggs on a bed of cabbage, with egg-drop soup and as much rice as you like; the dish has been on TV (Chachai-re Monday, per an October 2026 diner) and can sell out. At night the counter grills knuckle steak and serves dumplings, spring rolls and mapo tofu, and you can eat without drinking. One diner found the char siu too sweet and the afternoon beer served half-frozen (September 2026). Smoking is allowed in the evening.

osaka_osteria_gaudente_ekimae_dai4.notes: [Italian · Umeda, an osteria under the station buildings since 1998] A long-running Italian osteria in the basement of Osaka Ekimae Dai-4 Building, one of three Gaudente shops in Osaka and Kobe and a Tabelog Italian WEST 100 pick in 2021. The idea is an Italian izakaya: friendly staff, regional dishes "in true Italian portions" and wine from all over Italy (official site). Weekday lunch starts with pasta sets from ¥1,500, generous on seafood; since EXPO 2025 there is also a Serbian lunch of cheese or meat pies and cevapi from the Serbian Pavilion's restaurant. Dinner is a ¥4,880 prix-fixe or à la carte, and each autumn fresh porcini arrive from Italy for linguine, risotto or fritto (¥4,000, October 2026). It fills on Sundays, so book; diners praise the staff's memory and the handling of birthday-cake requests (October 2026).

osaka_sushibar_hanabi_grand_front.notes: [Sushi · Umekita, a sushi-and-wine counter in a food hall] A sushi bar on the UMEKITA FLOOR of Grand Front Osaka's North Building, a food hall where diners take a seat in the shared area and order from several counters, opened in November 2023. It pairs sushi with wine: a sommelier picks over 25 bottles, and even the sake comes in wine glasses. Lunch is the easy way in: ten pieces of sushi with miso soup for ¥1,680 (October 2026), seafood bowls, or sets with a mini udon or chawanmushi. At night order sushi one piece at a time or take a course with tempura and grilled yellowtail collar from ¥3,500. Reviews call the fish fresh and the room calm, but one July 2026 diner found the rice firm and the chawanmushi bland. It is one of the 魚萬 group's restaurants.

osaka_sik_eatery_grand_green.notes: [Dim sum · Umekita Park, a park café of dim sum] A bright café-restaurant in a pavilion of Umekita Park at Grand Green Osaka, next to the Waldorf Astoria, opened in September 2024; the other SIK eatery is by Utsubo Park. The concept is a Chinese restaurant a woman can walk into alone (official site): dim sum by a chef from well-known restaurants, Chinese, Hong Kong and Taiwanese small plates, and natural wine. Lunch is the favourite: a bowl of gentle congee with three steaming dim sum for ¥1,430, or Hainan chicken rice, ordered by QR code. Dogs are welcome on the terrace and, at set hours, inside; at weekends it opens at 8:00. You can borrow a picnic set and take a bottle of wine into the park. Book for lunch; the room is small and popular.

osaka_jon_nacchi_kitahorie.notes: [Korean · Kitahorie, Busan-style nakkopse] A small Kitahorie shop, three minutes from Yotsubashi, devoted to nakkopse, the Busan hot pot of octopus, offal and shrimp in a bright red broth. Pick one of four spice levels (one diner found mild barely spicy, another regretted the hot one), eat it over rice with free refills of bean-sprout namul, seaweed and kimchi, and finish by frying rice in what is left, with cheese and flying-fish roe on top. Diners in 2026 singled out the sweet, tender offal and the crisp minari chijimi; there are plenty of makgeolli to drink. Orders go through your phone; the menu and some staff are in Korean. The room is small and seating is 90 minutes, so book. Closed Mondays.

osaka_shunsai_amanoi_nishishinsaibashi.notes: [Kaiseki · Nishi-Shinsaibashi, a hidden flat on the 9th floor] A reservation-only Japanese restaurant hidden in a flat on the ninth floor of an apartment building behind the Hotel Nikko, made over into tatami and table rooms for two up to 28, quiet enough that, the listing says, celebrities come incognito. The house dish is a Kyoto duck hot pot of duck raised in Kyotanba, finished with handmade soba (¥7,700 with all-you-can-drink in November 2025); otherwise take the ten-dish seasonal kaiseki, with thick-cut sashimi and steamed kinmedai. Diners praise the value and the staff, who dimmed the lights for elderly guests at one party (August 2026); one found the walls between rooms thin. Bookings are getting harder (April 2026); cancellations the day before are charged in full. Closed Sundays and holidays.

osaka_honru_santen_higashishinsaibashi.notes: [Taiwanese · Higashi-Shinsaibashi, the stone-pot hot pot] A long-running Taiwanese restaurant on a Higashi-Shinsaibashi corner, its walls lined with celebrity autographs, where regulars of ten and even thirty years come back for the stone-pot hot pot: pork, seafood, squid balls and vegetables stir-fried in sesame oil in front of you, then simmered in a gentle chicken-bone broth that diners drink by the bowl, with noodles to finish (¥4,730 a person with three starters). Do not skip the homemade oyster spring rolls, crisp outside and soft inside, the dried-radish omelette, or the shijimi clams steeped a week in house soy sauce. The chef trained at Tsuji Culinary Institute and in Taipei and Kaohsiung, and diners call the owner-chef friendly. Chinese spoken. Closed Sundays except in December.

osaka_sakanaza_maeda_higashishinsaibashi.notes: [French · Higashi-Shinsaibashi, a 30-year bistro] A small French restaurant up a flight of stairs east of the クリスタ長堀 underground mall, open for about 30 years by the staff's count and still cooking one omakase course of the season, booked two days ahead. In August 2026 that meant bright seasonal-vegetable appetizers, a cold soup in a big bowl, crisp-skinned fish and a tender steak; the 2024 menus ran to wild-boar gratin, stone bass with firefly squid and a sirloin-cap tartare. It is a place people return to for decades: one couple came back on the anniversary of a first date there 23 years before (2023), and business diners call it consistent. Lunch ran about ¥3,000–4,000 and dinner ¥10,000–15,000 with wine in 2026. Counter seats are comfortable for one. Closed Mondays.

osaka_centre_m_nishishinsaibashi.notes: [Italian · Nishi-Shinsaibashi, fresh-pasta lunch and afternoon tea in a hotel] The second-floor restaurant of the Tokyu Stay Mercure Osaka Namba, a calm room above a lobby busy with overseas travellers (October 2026), open from lunch through afternoon tea to dinner. The weekday lunch is the draw: pick one of a dozen fresh pastas, the noodles sent from Awaji Island each morning, and help yourself to the baker's breads, croissants of fermented butter, and six deli salads, soft drinks included, from ¥2,900. Afternoons are for seasonal afternoon tea (¥6,000 in autumn 2026, Shine Muscat and chestnut) and large fruit parfaits; evenings for set courses from ¥5,500, with a whole cake on the anniversary course. Diners praise the bread, the smiling staff and the value; the buffet can queue at busy times (June 2026).

osaka_manryo_nipponbashi.notes: [Yakiniku · Nipponbashi, whole-cattle A5 wagyu on a thick teppan, noon to midnight] The Nipponbashi branch of Manryo, a yakiniku name diners know from its other Osaka shops (reviewers mention Minami-Morimachi and Tenma), on Sakaisuji near Kuromon Market and open straight from noon to midnight. The beef is A5 black wagyu bought whole, so the menu reaches into rare cuts, and it cooks on a thick iron plate that you rub with beef fat as you go, with a printed guide to grilling times. Order the Nipponbashi-only negi shio tan, thick tongue under green-onion salt, then the phantom kalbi if it isn't sold out and the 20-second shabu-yaki loin dipped in egg; finish with stone-grilled bibimbap and the big clam-and-seaweed soup. A regular on an eighth visit (September 2026) calls the tongue a favourite. Lunch is quiet but at evening prices. One August 2026 diner missed an explanation of the grill and found the service mechanical; another was puzzled at first at cleaning the plate during the meal.

osaka_yakiniku_nandaimon_higashishinsaib.notes: [Yakiniku · Higashi-Shinsaibashi, a 1964 Shizuoka yakiniku's Osaka shop] The Osaka outpost, opened in 2019, of a Shizuoka yakiniku founded in 1964 and, per its Tabelog text, popular with baseball and soccer players. A lively, old-style room near Nagahoribashi with a counter, tables and a shoes-off tatami area, where you grill domestic black wagyu chosen by the owner over charcoal shichirin in rising smoke. The thick-cut tongue steak is limited to ten a day; diners in 2026 also praise the thick, tender negi tan shio, the premium outside skirt, the toro yukhoe and the choice of kimchi, and finish with the house cold noodles and makgeolli. Portions are generous and drinks are on the dear side (August 2026); one September 2026 diner found the cuts too fatty. Smoking is allowed, and booking is wise.

osaka_anngon_minamisenba.notes: [Vietnamese · Minami-Semba, pho and spring rolls since 1998] A Vietnamese restaurant up a narrow stair near Shinsaibashi, open since 1998 and cooked by a Vietnamese chef, Tam, in a room dressed with things brought from Vietnam to evoke the Mekong's garden restaurants. Lunch fills fast: choose one of nine pho or noodle bowls with a rice dish (¥1,300), or the ¥1,950 healthy set of fresh and fried spring rolls, chicken pho, green-papaya salad and chè, and ask for more coriander, which is free. The fresh spring rolls of shrimp and pork are the house signature, one October 2026 diner's best in Osaka; at night come in a group for duck hot pot, goat or stir-fried pork tongue. Some find it tuned to Japanese tastes; one September 2026 diner lost a bowl of broth cleared too fast.

osaka_unzen_sanbangai.notes: [Teppan skewers · Umeda, Hankyu Sanbangai B2F] A cosy counter-and-tables shop in the Hankyu Sanbangai basement, from Unzen, a Kitashinchi skewer house that diners date to 1950. Skewers of meat, seafood and vegetables are cooked on a teppan rather than over charcoal, splashed with dashi, and set down two at a time beside the sauce that suits each one: plum soy, the house sauce, sesame miso or salt. It runs all day with one menu, so a ¥2,000 course of six skewers with salad, rice and miso soup works as a late lunch, and a ¥1,500 set of three skewers and a drink as a quick stop. Booking ahead earns small extras like a sorbet or an extra skewer. Several 2026 reviews mention attentive staff from overseas who explain each skewer. Quiet on some weekend afternoons.

osaka_tachinomi_osaka_fugutaro.notes: [Fugu · Umeda, a standing fugu bar] A second-floor standing bar a minute from Hankyu Umeda that sells domestic tiger fugu at drinking-bar prices: tessa sashimi from about ¥500, a hot pot just under ¥1,000 and a rice-porridge finish, plus fugu skin, kara-age, tempura and nigiri. The owner, 島本 一樹, opened it in September 2025 at 39 after appearing on the TV pitch show Reiwa no Tora, wanting fugu to be an everyday dish rather than a special-occasion one (official site). Sake runs to 30–40 kinds with a cheap all-you-can-drink, and the chilled fin sake is a favourite. Diners found the fugu as good as at a regular fugu restaurant (October 2026) and the owner friendly. No seats, no courses; an hour after work is the idea. Closed Thursdays.

osaka_kusunoki_fusae_honten_ekimae2.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. The menu includes fried dishes (kakiage, kisu tempura, fried sardine cake), shumai, dote-yaki in a sweet miso sauce and oden; soy and miso seasonings normally contain wheat.
osaka_kusunoki_fusae_honten_ekimae2.vegan_detail: Not vegan: an izakaya of sashimi, fried fish, pork, beef and dashi-based obanzai and oden.
osaka_kusunoki_fusae_honten_ekimae2.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 16:00–23:00; Sat 14:00–23:00; holidays 14:00–22:00; last order food 22:00, drinks 22:30 (21:00/21:30 on holidays); Sunday closed per the hours table, though the same listing also gives "Sun & Public Holidays 14:00–22:00" for this shop and はなれ; some Sundays and Mondays listed as closed in October (Tabelog). Same-day bookings by phone only; a 2-hour limit when busy; a table is released if you are more than 10 minutes late and cannot be reached (Tabelog). Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR; Osaka Premium Coupons accepted (Tabelog). No cover charge (Tabelog). 20 seats: a table for 6, three tables for 2, 8 at the counter (Tabelog). Smoking: the listing says the shop has been entirely smoke-free since February 2026, and elsewhere that smoking is allowed in the group's shops from February 2026; reviews in August and September 2026 describe it as non-smoking. Opened 18 June 2009 (Tabelog).
osaka_kusunoki_fusae_honten_ekimae2.notes: [Izakaya · Umeda, Osaka Station Front Building No. 2 B1F] A small sake-and-Japanese-food bar in the basement of Osaka Station Front Building No. 2, the main shop of a three-shop group in the station-front buildings (Tabelog). The cooking comes from a chef with thirty years behind the stove, the sake from a holder of a sake diploma, and the signature Fusae Set puts a little of everything on one tray, sashimi, tempura, meat and simmered dishes, with sea urchin and salmon roe as a ¥500 extra. Obanzai, oden, shumai and fried sardine cakes fill the board, and a ¥4,000 course with 90 minutes of drinks makes it an easy office party. Diners praise friendly, energetic staff; one July 2026 group was asked for last orders 90 minutes after sitting down. Cash only; book same-day by phone.

osaka_brasserie_la_loge_ibis_umeda.notes: [Hotel brasserie · Higashi-Umeda, ibis Osaka Umeda 1F] The ground-floor restaurant of the ibis Osaka Umeda hotel, reachable from the Whity Umeda underground mall, open to non-guests for breakfast, lunch and an afternoon café. Breakfast is a ¥2,000–2,200 Japanese-and-Western buffet with croissants from France and coffee to take away. Lunch pairs a main dish (braised wagyu, salmon, roast pork) with a half buffet of salads, soups and breads from ¥1,700, plus a ¥700 drink bar and a ¥300 dessert. The room is large and calm with sofas and Osaka-themed art. A July 2026 diner noted that most staff come from overseas and speak good Japanese; a September 2026 diner saw many European hotel guests. No lunch on Wednesdays.

osaka_mamagotoya_nishishinsaibashi.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information. A fish-led Japanese kitchen: sashimi, grilled eel and dobin-mushi sit beside tempura and dishes in dashi and soy-based sauces; nothing is described as gluten-free.
osaka_mamagotoya_nishishinsaibashi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: seasonal fish, eel, crab and beef, with dashi-based dishes throughout.

osaka_mamagotoya_nishishinsaibashi.notes: [Japanese · Shinsaibashi, a 1987 counter for seasonal à la carte] On the fifth floor of a building near Daimaru, a calm Japanese room with a fifteen-seat counter and two semi-private tatami rooms, open since 1987. One diner says the way to eat here is à la carte from a long seasonal list with no prices shown: in autumn 2026 dobin-mushi of matsutake and conger eel, crab with sweet potato, scallop and sea-urchin tempura, eel grilled two ways and Chateaubriand, finished with grilled rice balls and wasanbon ice cream; in summer, finely bone-cut hamo, ayu and wild eel. There is also a ¥12,000 seasonal course and a sake pairing, and staff explain each dish and suggest sake from around Japan. Old Western classics play in a Japanese room (June 2026). Used for business dinners and for entertaining overseas guests (October 2026). Closed Sundays.

osaka_amitie_shinsaibashi.gf_detail: Ask when booking. The site says courses are built around each guest's preferences and allergies, but nothing is called gluten-free; courses include bread, and the fish course at dinner comes in a donabe with a sauce meant for bread.
osaka_amitie_shinsaibashi.vegan_detail: Ask when booking. Vegetables from contract farms open every course and the site promises courses adjusted to preferences, but the courses are built on fish and meat (wagyu, venison, Iberico pork) and no vegan menu is listed.
osaka_amitie_shinsaibashi.hours_raw: Tue–Sun lunch 11:30–14:30 (last order 13:30; 13:00 at weekends), dinner 17:00–21:30 (last order 19:30; 21:00 close on Sundays and holidays); closed Monday (the next day when Monday is a holiday) and one irregular day a month (official site; Tabelog); November 2026 closures listed for the 2nd, 5th, 9th, 16th, 18th, 24th and 30th (official site). Only Christmas courses 19–26 December (official site), when Tabelog asks that children of elementary age and under not come. Prices include tax and a 10% service charge (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners, UnionPay) and QR (PayPay, d Barai, Rakuten Pay, au PAY); no e-money (Tabelog). 26 seats (Tabelog; 28 on the official site), tables set apart, semi-private curtained spaces for 2 to 8; non-smoking, smoking on the terrace; wheelchair accessible; children welcome, children's plate ¥2,800 booked ahead, no high chairs or changing tables (Tabelog). On the 6th floor; the lift is at the back of the building (September 2026).
osaka_amitie_shinsaibashi.notes: [French · Shinsaibashi, a 1980 hideaway above the arcade] A minute from Daimaru, up a lift at the back of a building to the sixth floor, a French restaurant founded in 1980 that calls itself a hideaway for 45 years. The site's promise is a relaxed room rather than hotel formality, and the second-generation owner 下村 runs it with chef 中川. Courses open with a plate of rare vegetables from contract farms, each explained at the table, then fish sent straight from the market (cooked in a donabe at dinner) and meat such as wagyu or venison, with foie gras as an extra; repeat guests are promised different dishes. Lunch from ¥4,000, dinner from ¥6,000, tax and service included. Popular for birthdays and anniversaries: diners in 2026 describe messages written on dessert plates, photos taken at the table and a celebration plate for a wedding. Closed Mondays and one other day a month.

chef_bio.background: Per the official site: the founder joined 志摩観光ホテル at 賢島 in Mie, gained service experience at a French restaurant in Osaka, and founded Amitie in 1980 with a dozen-odd seats, moving into this building's 6th floor when it was completed in 1988. The second-generation owner keeps the founder's idea of a relaxed place for real French food, alongside a chef "who loves food and wine too much". Vegetables come from contract farms that build the soil to grow Italian vegetables; wagyu and venison are carefully handled to remove gaminess; fish arrives straight from the market. The site aims to build each course around the guest's tastes and allergies and to serve repeat guests different dishes.
chef_bio.philosophy: Not hotel-style formality but a relaxed room, kind-to-the-body ingredients and real French food; forget about manners, wine orders and dress codes (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Vegetable starter plates; fish in a donabe; anniversary courses.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (ami-gr1980.com): 1980年創業 フランス料理のお店、心斎橋 大丸より徒歩1分、ビル6階の隠れ家、隠れ続けて45年、店主 下村 シェフ 中川。どんなお店: 三重県賢島の志摩観光ホテルに入社後、大阪のフランス料理店でサービスの経験を積み、1980年に「アミチェ」を創業、当初は10数席、1988年に今のビルができて移転、先代の気持ちを大切に2代目店主として、料理とワインが好きすぎるシェフと共に、契約農家の自然野菜、黒毛和牛や鹿肉、イベリコ豚、市場直送の魚、ディナーの魚料理は土鍋仕立て、記念日コースはデザートの皿にメッセージ、好みやアレルギーを考慮してコースを作る、2回目以降は違った料理を。ランチ: フルコースランチ5,000円 (通常6,000円、ネット予約)、シェフおまかせコース A 9,500円・B 12,500円・C 16,500円、デジュネ4,000円 (数量・曜日限定)。ディナー: シェフおまかせコース A 9,500円・B 12,500円・C 16,500円、グルマンコース8,000円 (ネット限定)、ムニュ・ボヌール7,500円、プチ・ボヌール6,000円。店舗情報: ラ・シーンビル6F、ランチ L.O. 13時30分、ディナー L.O. 19時30分、21時30分閉店、月曜定休 (祝日の場合は翌日) と不定休月1回、28席、カーテンスペース2〜8名、各種カードと QR 決済。クリスマス (12月19日〜26日) は限定コースのみ。食べログ (店舗会員): フレンチ、税・サービス料10%込み、26席、半個室、禁煙 (テラスで喫煙可)、車椅子可、お子様プレート2,800円、ソムリエ。口コミ(2026年6月〜10月): 珍しい野菜の前菜を一つずつ説明、ウニとトマトのジュレ、玉ねぎのポタージュ、栗のスープ、熟成した鹿肉、フォアグラの追加、デザートにお祝いのメッセージ、写真を撮ってくれる、エレベーターは奥。

The Sunday lunch draws a queue: 5 to 10 or more people before 11:30, and an hour's wait for later arrivals (May–June 2026); evenings can be quiet (June 2026). osaka_shinmachi_sobakiri_teruteru.notes: [Soba · Shinmachi, a couple's soba bar for sake and noodles] A calm, clean Japanese-modern room on a Shinmachi street, run by a couple (as diners in 2022 and June 2026 describe it), with a few counter seats, tables and a small raised area, and jazz playing. The soba is the point: up to five kinds a day, from white, delicate sarashina to dark coarse-ground inaka, with 100% buckwheat (十割) costing the same as the 80/20 blend (二八), and a sign at the door saying there are no rice dishes. Evenings are for sake and small plates first (itawasa with sea-urchin miso, fiery karami daikon, firefly squid, sobagaki, dashimaki), then a plate of cold soba from ¥950. Lunch is Sundays only, with a queue before 11:30. Open Thursday to Sunday evenings; book for the 18:00 start.

Saba sushi to take away, including next morning (August 2026).
osaka_abaraya_sennichimae.notes: [Sushi · Ura Namba, an old sushi house famous for battera] Tucked into a back alley behind Namba Grand Kagetsu, a three-storey sushi house with a genuine retro feel, a counter downstairs and tatami rooms above, which an August 2026 diner dates to 1955. It is known above all for saba sushi: a battera with a leaf on top and a hint of sansho, eaten without soy sauce, ten pieces even as a half order, and sold to take away. The ¥4,400 course runs from sashimi and chawanmushi through simmered sea bream and tempura to the saba sushi; à la carte there are tuna and salmon sashimi, tekka maki, dobin-mushi in autumn and steamed sea-bream bones. One regular was on a 45th visit in October 2026; another found the place empty on a Saturday night and called it too well hidden. Prices are modest. Closed Sundays and holidays.

osaka_kamatake_udon_shin_osaka.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat udon, with tempura toppings (chikuwa, soft-boiled egg, chicken, maitake) and a bonito dashi or bukkake sauce.
osaka_kamatake_udon_shin_osaka.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a bonito dashi (October 2026) and toppings of chikuwa, egg, chicken and beef.
osaka_kamatake_udon_shin_osaka.hours_raw: Daily except Tuesday 11:00–15:00 (last order 14:30), holidays included (Tabelog; reopened 2 September 2025 after a break). The listing notes also say "closed on Wednesdays", which contradicts its own table; check before going. Buy a ticket at the machine outside first; cash, or PayPay if you call the staff out to the machine (September and October 2026). 9 counter seats; non-smoking (Tabelog). Lunch lines of five to ten are usual on weekdays, with waits of 5–10 minutes; one person cooks and serves, so the next group goes in only when seats are cleared (September–October 2026).
osaka_kamatake_udon_shin_osaka.notes: [Udon · Shin-Osaka Station, a one-person Sanuki counter] A nine-seat udon counter at the end of the 味の小路 food alley under the Shin-Osaka tracks, outside the ticket gates, from the Kamatake udon shops that a July 2026 diner calls famous in Minami. One person makes, boils and serves every bowl (2026). The order is the chiku-tama tempura bukkake (¥880): glossy, neatly folded noodles, chewy but smooth, under a big crisp chikuwa tempura and a runny soft-boiled egg tempura, with ginger, green onion and lemon, cold or hot. Meat bukkake with wagyu and maitake tempura (¥1,350) and kasu udon (¥930) are the richer choices. Buy your ticket at the machine before joining the line; lunchtime waits are short but steady. Lunch only, closed Tuesdays. A good stop between trains.

osaka_tai_paitan_ramen_marusankaku_shin_.notes: [Ramen · Shin-Osaka west, sea-bream paitan in a kaiseki-like room] A 15-seat ramen shop five minutes from the Shin-Osaka subway exit, open since 2018 and in Tabelog's Ramen 100 every year from 2023 to 2025, where everything is built on sea bream. The tai paitan is blended at the counter (one diner saw the bow-tied chef finish it with a blender) into a thick, creamy, "liquid sea bream" broth over medium-thin noodles, and the special bowl adds kombu-cured sea-bream slices, a smoked egg, fried burdock and menma cut into the ○ and ▽ of the name (¥1,460). There is a clear sea-bream soup too, tsukemen, and sea-bream rice to finish with the broth. The room is designed like a kaiseki restaurant, and the staff are attentive. On one October 2026 evening most of the customers were from overseas. Cash only.

The owner hums along to the shop's own song while cooking (June 2026). Cash only; check it is Thursday.

Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners, UnionPay), IC cards and other e-money, QR payment including Alipay and WeChat Pay (Tabelog). 20 seats: a counter of 12 and one counter table of 8; non-smoking (Tabelog). osaka_oden_to_ajifurai_barchika03.notes: [Oden · Umeda, oden and fried horse mackerel over the station] A neon-lit counter on the fifth floor of Innogate Osaka, straight off the JR west exit, the second shop of an oden bar in Honmachi (Tabelog). It does two things: oden simmered in a golden Kansai dashi (daikon, beef tendon, a soft egg, sesame tofu and a pouch stuffed with condiments that diners single out), and palm-sized fried horse mackerel from Sakai Port, thick, with coarse crumbs, a choice of tartar, mentaiko tartar or salt and lemon, and its fried bones on the side. Weekend doors open at 11:30 for daytime drinking; evenings fill, so book. One June 2026 group found it a little pricey for the size (¥14,300 for four); most diners in 2026 call the fish a must-order.

osaka_kawakyu_ekimae_dai3.notes: [Kaiseki · Umeda, Japanese food 142 m up] A large Japanese restaurant on the 33rd floor of Osaka Ekimae Dai-3 Building, 142 m above Umeda, where the windows look east to the Ikoma mountains and west toward the Akashi Strait (Tabelog). Twelve private rooms with sunken kotatsu seating hold groups of five to fifty, which makes it a favourite for business dinners and family celebrations. Lunch is good value: a three-tier makunouchi bento of sashimi, simmered dishes and tempura for ¥1,980 (September 2026), or tempura and gozen sets. In the evening the monthly Kawakyu kaiseki runs from seasonal starters and sashimi to takikomi rice. Reviews are kind about the view and the price and mixed on the cooking, which some found average, with small windows in some private rooms and noisy clearing of plates (October 2026). Closed Mondays.

osaka_kushiage_kanayama_kitashinchi.notes: [Kushiage · Kitashinchi, skewers and aged-pork katsu] A calm basement kushiage counter on Kitashinchi's main street, opened in 2019, where the cook breads and fries skewers of organic vegetables, domestic meat and seafood in front of a crescent-shaped counter, with private rooms for two or four. Dinner is a ten-skewer course or an omakase that runs until you call stop (¥8,800–10,000), ending with jako rice and red miso soup. Lunch is the bargain and the reason most reviewers come: tonkatsu of snow-room-aged pork, loin and fillet from ¥1,700, a minced-meat cutlet filled with foie gras (¥2,400), shiso rice refilled free and a small bowl of grated yam with wasabi to cut the fat. Book lunch; it fills by 13:00. Closed Sundays.

osaka_capi_kitashinchi.notes: [Italian · Kitashinchi, an eight-seat innovative counter] A small counter on the sixth floor of the Kitashinchi PLACE building where an owner-chef cooks one omakase of Italian-rooted dishes built on pairing ingredients, with a sommelier's wines from around the world. The listing says it has held a Michelin star in Kyoto and Osaka every year since 2022, and Tabelog named it an Innovative 100 in 2025. Diners remember the house brioche, the caviar with squid and cauliflower, Kyoto Nanatani duck and the "explosive seafood", a baked crab risotto; two 2025 diners note the chef came from Ponte Vecchio and find the cooking closer to classic Italian than avant-garde. The course is ¥26,000–31,000 plus 10% service; with pairing expect about ¥50,000 (January 2026). Two seatings a night; book ahead. Steak Ron is on the ground floor of the same building.

osaka_live_yakiniku_tengu_sennichimae.notes: [Yakiniku · Sennichimae, until 5 a.m.] A yakiniku house under a giant tengu sign between Namba and Nippombashi, where staff cut each order of meat at the counter and the portions run 1.5 to 2 times the usual. The tongue is the order: a platter of several kinds, salted, with the harami, mino and a yukke. Book for a table upstairs, or walk in for the downstairs counter and watch the knife work; stays are 90 minutes. Open until 5 a.m. six nights a week. A free ice-cream monaka ends the meal. Diners in 2026 paid about ¥5,000–10,000 a head; two August 2026 diners report different yukke prices (¥2,200 and ¥1,500). Many guests were visitors from overseas (August 2026).

chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog shop text: meat chosen each day by experienced professionals, cut to order and served fresh, in portions over 1.5 times a typical yakiniku restaurant's, with Special A rank rice. osaka_mukaka_shinmachi.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. Straw- and charcoal-grilled meat and fish come with soy-based condiments, and the menu also has pasta, pizza and fried horse mackerel; nothing is described as gluten-free.
osaka_mukaka_shinmachi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the menu is built on straw-grilled bonito, chicken and beef and a meat-heavy appetiser platter.
osaka_mukaka_shinmachi.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 17:00–22:30; Sat, Sun and holidays 15:00–22:30; closed irregularly; hours may be cut short when dishes sell out, so call ahead (Tabelog). Reservations recommended, with a two-hour limit; a booking is cancelled at 10 minutes late without a call; tell the staff in advance about children (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). Service charge ¥250 a person (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) and PayPay; no e-money (Tabelog). 28 seats: a counter of 6 and tables; non-smoking, though the room fills with smoke from the smoking and straw grilling (Tabelog; September 2026).
osaka_mukaka_shinmachi.notes: [Izakaya · Shinmachi, straw fire and a box of small plates] A busy, smoky izakaya in Shinmachi where a chef who came from a popular restaurant grills meat and fish over burning straw and charcoal, and adds a little Italian. Everyone orders the Mukamori, a wooden box of more than ten small appetisers for at least two, which is enough to fill two people on its own, so share it and add only the straw-grilled bonito, a pasta or a pizza. Book ahead (stays are two hours); weekends open at 15:00. Expect ¥4,000–6,000 a head plus a ¥250 service charge.

roles: Chef who worked at a popular restaurant, unnamed (Tabelog shop text)
chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog shop text: straw-grilled and charcoal-grilled dishes by a chef who worked at a popular restaurant; quick straw smoking adds aroma to meat and fish; a few Italian dishes; seasonal recommendations and the day's fish grilled over straw.
chef_bio.specialty: Mukamori appetiser box; straw-grilled bonito.

anecdotes.text: "The Mukaka Assortment was truly generous in portion size, packed with over 10 types of appetizers in a wooden box." — September 2026.
"The grilled bonito had a wonderful aroma from the straw grilling, and I could enhance the flavors with toppings like green onions, wasabi, sprouts, and garlic chips." — October 2026.
"I visited for an early dinner, and the 3 PM opening time was a great help." — August 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (店舗会員): ムカカ (mukaka)、居酒屋・イタリアン・創作料理、大阪市西区新町1-11-11 スカイハイツSAWA 1F、西大橋駅2番出口、本町駅23番出口、四ツ橋駅2番出口から徒歩5分、月〜金17:00〜22:30、土・日・祝15:00〜22:30、不定休、売り切れで早く閉めることも、予約は2時間制、10分遅れて連絡がなければ取り消し、子ども連れは事前に、サービス料1名250円、カード・PayPay 可、28席 (カウンター6、テーブル22)、禁煙、人気店出身の料理人の藁焼きと炭火焼き、イタリアンも少し、名物「Mukamori」、4名からの3,000円のコース (飲み放題は2,000円追加)。口コミ(2025年9月〜2026年10月): 10種以上の前菜の木箱の盛り合わせは2人前からで量が多い、燻製のポテトサラダ、鶏のハラミ、藁焼きの鰹、ピザ、パスタ、煙が多い、予約は必須。

osaka_shinsaibashi_baisenjo.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. Coffee aside, the food is taiyaki, chiffon cake, Basque cheesecake and pudding; the pudding is the item without obvious flour, but nothing is stated about it.
osaka_shinsaibashi_baisenjo.vegan_detail: Ask. No vegan information. Black coffee is the plain option; ask about plant milk for lattes. The cakes, pudding and taiyaki fillings use dairy and eggs or are not described.
osaka_shinsaibashi_baisenjo.hours_raw: Sources disagree on the hours: Tabelog gives daily 9:00–18:30, and a diner came at just after 9:00 on a June 2026 Friday; the official site gives 11:00–19:00. Check before an early or late visit. No reservations (Tabelog). Order downstairs, then sit upstairs; eating in needs one drink each (2026 reviews). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) for ¥1,000 and over, transport IC and PayPay (Tabelog). 24 seats on the skylit second floor; non-smoking; take-out; children welcome (Tabelog; official site). Opened 15 January 2015 (Tabelog).
osaka_shinsaibashi_baisenjo.notes: [Café · Shinsaibashi, a roastery with taiyaki] A wood-clad roastery with a silver chimney just off the main street by Shinsaibashi Station, roasting beans downstairs and serving them upstairs in a skylit room. Order at the counter, then climb to the second floor; the baristas will suggest beans to your taste, and lattes come with latte art. The building also holds a taiyaki and a chiffon-cake counter, so a coffee comes with a crisp taiyaki, a bacon-cheese taiyaki breakfast plate, an Earl Grey chiffon cake or a salted Basque cheesecake. The two sources differ on hours (Tabelog 9:00–18:30; official site 11:00–19:00), and a latte cost ¥550 in September 2026 and ¥650 in October.

roles: Operator: Garden Bar & Coffee Japan (official site)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: a roastery where green beans chosen from around the world are roasted in front of customers and blended by top Japanese baristas, with a CIMBALI espresso machine and a calm skylit café on the second floor; opened in Shinsaibashi for the many kinds of people who pass through; the operator also runs Welcome the Coffee. Reviewers note that the taiyaki and chiffon cake counters in the same building appear to be run by the same company (2026). Opened 15 January 2015 (Tabelog).
chef_bio.philosophy: To let many people know and enjoy the real aroma and taste of coffee (official site, translated).
chef_bio.specialty: House-roasted coffee; taiyaki and chiffon cake with coffee.

anecdotes.text: "I mentioned that I'm not a fan of bitter coffee, and the staff recommended the Rwandan iced coffee. It had a refreshing acidity" — October 2026, with an espresso chiffon cake.
"A business card-sized paper explaining that today's coffee is from the Colombia Monserrate region was attached" — August 2026, a ¥750 cold brew to take away.
"You secure a seat on the 2nd floor and then place your order on the 1st floor." — June 2026, just after 9 AM on a Friday.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (ガーデンバール＆コーヒージャパン): 心斎橋焙煎所、木の壁から銀色の煙突が突き出た外観、店内の焙煎機、目の前で焼き上げるコーヒー豆、国内トップクラスのバリスタのブレンドの自家焙煎の豆、世界中から厳選した生豆、ラテアート、CIMBALI のエスプレッソマシン、日替わりのドリップコーヒー、キャラメルマキアート・蜂蜜カプチーノ・チャイモカなどのフレーバーラテ、2階は天窓の自然光の落ち着いたカフェ、OPEN 11:00〜CLOSE 19:00、大阪市中央区西心斎橋1-10-1、2026年秋のかぼちゃプリン、林檎とキャラメルのアップサイドダウンケーキ、Welcome the Coffee も運営。食べログ: 毎日9:00〜18:30、予約不可、カードは1,000円以上、交通系IC・PayPay 可、24席、禁煙、テイクアウト、2015年1月15日オープン。口コミ(2026年6月〜10月): 1階で注文して2階の席へ、イートインはワンドリンク、たい焼きとシフォンケーキの店と同じ建物、ベーコンチーズたい焼きのモーニング、バスクチーズケーキ800円、カフェラテ550円 (2026年9月) と650円 (2026年10月)、コールドブリュー750円、ルワンダ、海外の客も。

cultural_comfort.note: Order at the counter downstairs; baristas suggest beans to your taste (2026); many overseas visitors (June 2026). No English evidence found.

osaka_yakiniku_yushun_minamisenba.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. Much of the meat is eaten with salt or sesame salt, but there is a house sauce and a miso sauce, and the menu has cold noodles and tail soup; nothing is described as gluten-free.
osaka_yakiniku_yushun_minamisenba.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a black-wagyu yakiniku menu of tongue, harami and horumon; kimchi and namul assortments are the plant dishes mentioned.
osaka_yakiniku_yushun_minamisenba.hours_raw: Mon, Tue and Thu–Sun 17:00–23:00 (last order 22:30); closed Wednesday (Tabelog). Reservations accepted; call for same-day bookings; booked out on some weekday nights (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners, UnionPay), PayPay and Alipay; no e-money (Tabelog). 48 seats: mostly counter on 1F, tables on 2F for groups up to 35; non-smoking; sports viewing; free Wi-Fi; children and strollers welcome (Tabelog; July 2026 review).
osaka_yakiniku_yushun_minamisenba.notes: [Yakiniku · Minamisenba, black-wagyu tongue and horumon] A two-floor yakiniku room in Minamisenba, counter downstairs under signed memorabilia that a July 2026 diner took for signatures of baseball players, tables upstairs, that buys selected black wagyu for its tongue and harami and serves a long list of fresh wagyu horumon. Diners point to the special salted tongue, the tsurami and harami, and the thin chuck-eye roll eaten with sesame salt; the sauces are light. Book, even on weekdays, and expect ¥6,000–15,000 a head in 2026. Closed Wednesdays.

roles: Operator named in a July 2026 review: "Louis Valiant Co., Ltd., led by Nagisa Asai as the General Manager" (not checked elsewhere)
chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog shop text: carefully selected black-haired wagyu, wagyu only for the tongue and harami, a homemade sauce, fresh wagyu horumon; second-floor tables for banquets of up to 35. A July 2026 diner saw signed memorabilia, apparently of baseball players, above the first-floor counter.
chef_bio.specialty: Black-wagyu special salted tongue; wagyu horumon.

anecdotes.text: "This restaurant seems to favor salt-based sauces, and the staff recommended enjoying the meat with sesame salt." — July 2026, a same-day booking on a business trip.
"I highly recommend the 'Special Salted Tongue of Black-haired Wagyu.' … You get a satisfying portion of six large pieces." — July 2026.
"The liver here is particularly delicious—I ordered two plates." — April 2026, a fifth visit.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (店舗会員): 焼肉 優駿、焼肉・ホルモン・居酒屋、大阪市中央区南船場4-14-1 南船場センター1・2F、心斎橋駅からクリスタ長堀12番出口北へ徒歩5分、本町駅から7分ほど、月・火・木〜日17:00〜23:00 (L.O. 22:30)、水曜休み、予約可、当日は電話で、カード (銀聯も)・PayPay・Alipay 可、48席、2階のテーブルは35名まで、禁煙、スポーツ観戦、無料 Wi-Fi、子ども・ベビーカー可、厳選した黒毛和牛、タンとハラミは和牛のみ、自家製のタレ、新鮮な和牛ホルモン。口コミ(2026年4月〜10月): 黒毛和牛の特上塩タン6枚、タン盛り、tsurami、ハラミ、シャトーブリアン、ロース、ゴマ塩で食べるリブ芯の薄切り、タン刺し、センマイ刺しと味噌ダレ、塩ホルモン盛り、テールスープ、冷麺、1階のカウンターの上に野球選手らしいサイン、タレは軽め、平日でも予約がおすすめ。
